drift: D3.0 tentative: from electoral aggregates to fantasy incentive mechanisms and collective forecasting

A.question: Is there a legally reusable, timestamped independent dataset containing forecast histories, resolutions, and varying game-like scoring incentives allowing an observable PFL-specific mechanism test?
A.unit: forecast question × forecast time × platform / tournament
A.exposure: prospective game scoring/reputation incentive vs comparable no-scoring regime
A.true_outcome: out-of-sample forecast quality and participation diversity
A.interference: social feedback and leaderboard changes peer behavior

rivals: Incentive/reputational feedback improves timely information aggregation
incentives increase herding/selection and do not improve accuracy

C.design: Public-source rights and scientific-priority gate before touching any question-level outcomes; require documented license permitting analysis, historical prediction snapshots, resolution, timestamp and comparable incentive variation. If any missing, STOP_LOCAL.
controls: forecast market or expert-pool benchmark at identical timestamps
C.falsator: Unavailable rights/history or only published established effect

D.instrumentation: Read official API terms, academic priority literature, dataset download feasibility; record URLs/access and avoid storing personal forecaster profiles
D.QA: distinguish platform access vs rights to analyze/model; no missing=zero
